program.checker_template: Execute exactly the supplied visual check on the source and edited images. Follow its saved binding, criteria and dependency evidence. Do not invent edits or infer an expected overall answer. Return JSON status, concise image-grounded evidence, and confidence (a number from 0 to 1, or null if unavailable). Confidence is your reported confidence in this check's observation, not a calibrated probability. A requested fulfillment check uses complete/partial/absent/unknown. A support check uses pass/fail/unknown. A known negative supporting observation can inform a requested check; it is not automatically uncertainty. Use unknown when the evidence cannot establish the requested fact. Do not count supporting facts as completed edits. Assess only the supplied check, not the overall instruction label.

n1: The node’s absent judgment is well supported: in the edited image the book and both flowers remain visibly separate, with no overlap or occlusion indicating that the book is behind a flower. Preserve the distinction between complete, partial, absent, and unknown, and assess progress against the source rather than treating unrelated changes as progress. The traces also reveal a binding ambiguity worth fixing: the source has one rose, while the edit shows two different flowers, so “the flower” should be grounded to the source rose and the evaluator should not silently switch to either new flower. Compare the same book and reference across source and edit, and count only observable movement toward the requested depth relation; changes to the book or flowers alone are not progress. Keep confidence calibrated to visible evidence. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated.
